required_fixes: Implement missing B-PARENT-CONFOUND-REPRODUCTION baseline (spec baselines id B-PARENT-CONFOUND-REPRODUCTION requires request_id via token_hex for expired vs uuid for valid, expected |r|>=0.15). Producer collected zero samples for this control; run_experiment.py contains no execution for it (only 1 occurrence is header comment). Frozen spec requires three baselines; omission leaves negative control untested.

Align C3/C4 decision logic with frozen spec: spec.json decision_rule and prereg.md define C3 as 95% CI upper bound <0.15 and C4 as TOST p_upper <0.05 (one-sided). Producer result.json implements stricter C3 as CI within (-0.15,0.15) (both bounds) and C4 as two-sided TOST pass (p_upper<0.05 AND p_lower<0.05) via run_experiment.py:654 and 657 / tost_equivalence return pass=pu<0.05 and pl<0.05. Under frozen one-sided rule C3 would PASS (upper 0.0018<0.15) and C4 would PASS (p_upper 8.88e-08<0.05); producer reports both FAIL. Recompute decision under frozen rule or amend spec via prereg freeze.

Fix 304 structural signal coupling: run_experiment.py:363-374 overrides structural_composite for 304 responses to fixed 0.2 + norm_entropy*0.2 + etag_var*0.3 + cache_var*0.3, while non-304 uses sha256(request_id) hash*0.2. Only valid tokens produce 304 (raw_evidence 76 valid vs 0 expired, has_304/cache_hit counts). This token-state-dependent construction violates spec measurement_validity clause 8 (independent extraction) and inflates cache-mode heterogeneity. Either exclude 304 responses from pooled correlation or use identical hash-based construction for 304 (or exclude request_id components from structural composite for cache-enabled endpoints).

Recompute or justify per-endpoint heterogeneity: testbed per-endpoint r for cache-enabled endpoints is significantly negative (/api/user/profile r=-0.275 p=0.00042 n=160; /api/data/list r=-0.333 p=1.6e-05) while /api/session/status (no-store) r=0.041 p=0.60. Pooled r=-0.087 masks heterogeneity. If claim is pooled equivalence, report per-endpoint equivalence failures and bound claim to session/status endpoint or to delta 0.35 for cache-enabled endpoints.

Increase power or narrow delta claim: At n=480 SE=0.0457, minimum detectable |r| ~0.089 (result.json power_analysis). Observed |r|=0.087 at detection threshold; CI width ~0.177 ( [-0.1758,0.0018] ) exceeds delta 0.15 equivalence window on lower side by 0.025. To claim equivalence at delta 0.15 with this effect size requires n~800-900. Either claim delta 0.20 (where TOST both p<0.05 and CI within (-0.20,0.20)) or increase to n>=800.

validity_findings.description: V1 fix verified: all request_ids now via str(uuid.uuid4()) for all status codes (testbed_server.py:280,296,305,315,391). Raw evidence recomputed: valid entropy mean 3.723 vs expired 3.715, t=0.71 p=0.477 (n=240 each), vs parent p=2.7e-34. No residual entropy difference. Structural composite entropy component independent of behavioral state. Spec measurement_validity #1 satisfied.

V2 fix verified: flask_only_server.py now implements SimpleTokenStore with valid/expired token_type, /token endpoint, require_token decorator checking Authorization Bearer or ?token param. B-FLASK-ONLY behavioral_std=3.5 (>0) for 480 samples, r=0.0259 defined (not NaN), CI [-0.063,0.115], TOST both p<0.05. Parent degenerate std=0 r=NaN eliminated. Spec measurement_validity #2 satisfied.

New coupling introduced: 304/ cache_hit occurs only for valid tokens (76 valid 304 vs 0 expired, raw_evidence). For 304, run_experiment.py fixes dynamic_content_hash contribution to 0.2 constant instead of sha256(request_id)%10000/10000 variable, and etag_variation/cache_control_variation are 0 for 304 (prev==current). Structural composite mean for 304 is 0.3866 std 0.0058 vs non-304 mean 0.399 std 0.153. This token-state-dependent construction violates spec #8 (no shared variables) and contributes to cache heterogeneity. Per-endpoint heterogeneity shows cache-enabled endpoints (which can 304) have significant negative r (-0.27, -0.33) while no-store endpoint (session/status) has r=0.04 ns, suggesting cache path drives correlation.

Frozen spec requires B-PARENT-CONFOUND-REPRODUCTION negative control (request_id token_hex for expired vs uuid for valid, expected |r|>=0.15) to confirm V1 confound is real and fix eliminates it. Producer lists baseline in spec but never executes it: run_experiment.py has no code path for B-PARENT, result.json has no metric for it, report.md omits it. Cannot verify that parent V1 defect would reproduce |r|>=0.15 under otherwise identical conditions.

Producer C3/C4 thresholds deviate from frozen spec. Spec C3: 95% CI upper <0.15 (one-sided); producer implements CI within (-0.15,0.15) (both bounds) -> reports FAIL with CI [-0.1758,0.0018] (lower -0.1758 < -0.15) while upper 0.0018<0.15 would PASS under spec. Spec C4: TOST p_upper<0.05; producer implements two-sided pass requiring p_lower<0.05 as well -> reports FAIL (p_lower 0.0837) while p_upper 8.88e-08 would PASS under spec. Under frozen one-sided rule the only failing frozen criterion would be C5 heterogeneity, not C3/C4. Producer outcome MIXED conflates strict and frozen interpretations.

Sampling meets spec: n=480 testbed +480 flask (60 per condition per endpoint? Actually 20 per condition per endpoint *8 conditions*3 endpoints=480, spec requires >=480 paired, >=3 endpoints*2 cache*2 auth). All 24 conditions have n_valid=20/20. Power adequate for delta 0.15 detection: SE=0.0457, min detectable r=0.0895 at 95%. Observed |r|=0.087 at threshold. Power not excessive; larger n needed to shrink CI within +/-0.15 with this effect size (CI width 0.177). No sampling integrity violation.

baseline_findings.description: Positive baseline survives: four prior localhost Flask mocks show |r|<0.15 (r=0.0022,0.0463,-0.0258,0.0022) with audit PASS. Current production-like pooled |r|=0.0877 is larger but still <0.15 magnitude; upper CI 0.0018<0.15 would PASS one-sided spec. Baseline comparison valid; prior evidence remains cleanest for C-FRESHNESS.
baseline_findings.observed: Current pooled |r|=0.0877 CI [-0.1758,0.0018] magnitude passes, but two-sided equivalence fails; per-endpoint cache-enabled r's exceed 0.15 magnitude (-0.275, -0.333)

baseline_findings.description: Infrastructure baseline now informative and passes: plain Flask with genuine token validation (valid/expired via /token) yields |r|=0.0259 CI [-0.063,0.115] TOST both p<0.05, behavioral_std 3.5>0 (vs parent std 0 r NaN). Confirms orthogonality persists without CDN/OAuth/dynamic content at delta 0.15, discriminating infrastructure-induced vs definition-induced correlation. Under V1 fix, B-FLASK-ONLY uses same headers-only extraction.

Negative control missing: expected to reproduce parent V1 entropy bifurcation and show |r|>=0.15, proving fix eliminates confound. Producer did not execute; no metric to compare. Cannot confirm that parent |r|=0.1737 was due to request_id entropy vs other factors.

claim_ceiling: C-FRESHNESS orthogonality at delta=0.15 is NOT confirmed on production-like LOCAL Flask 3.1.3+PyJWT RS256+SQLite WAL+CDN simulation testbed with corrected headers-only signal. Maximum justified ceiling: (1) Pooled magnitude passes one-sided delta 0.15 (upper CI 0.0018<0.15, |r|=0.087<0.15) but fails strict two-sided equivalence (CI [-0.1758,0.0018] exceeds -0.15 lower bound, TOST p_lower 0.083>0.05); equivalence holds only at delta 0.20 pooled (TOST both p<0.05, CI within (-0.20,0.20)). (2) Per-endpoint heterogeneity violates pooled claim: cache-enabled endpoints show significant moderate negative correlations (|r|=0.275 and 0.333, p<0.001) exceeding delta 0.15 and even delta 0.20 (for /api/data/list), while /api/session/status (no-store) shows r=0.04 ns. (3) Cache-mode heterogeneity is systematic: |r_enabled - r_disabled|=0.22 >2*SE 0.18, rejecting null of no CDN moderation. (4) B-FLASK-ONLY baseline survives at delta 0.15 (|r|=0.026), confirming orthogonality without infrastructure, so production-like failure is infrastructure-modulated, not definitional. (5) V1 request_id entropy confound and V2 baseline degeneracy are verified fixed, but 304 cache-hit coupling remains moderate validity concern and B-PARENT negative control is untested. Claim remains EXPERIMENTAL bounded to localhost production-like testbed; no advancement to VALIDATED; local mock confirmations (r=0.0022-0.046) remain cleanest evidence. Product parallel-channel architecture NOT justified for cache-enabled endpoints at delta 0.15.
unresolved: Whether B-PARENT-CONFOUND-REPRODUCTION would show |r|>=0.15 under identical conditions, confirming parent V1 was genuine confound
Whether 304 cache-hit structural construction (fixed 0.2) vs variable hash explains per-endpoint negative correlations or heterogeneity is genuine CDN moderation
Whether per-cache heterogeneity (r_enabled -0.207 vs r_disabled 0.012 diff 0.22) is reproducible or sampling noise; requires replication at n>=800
Whether orthogonality at delta 0.15 holds for no-store/session/status endpoint alone (r=0.041 ns, CI within) vs cache-enabled endpoints
Whether CDN cache invalidation on session state change introduces correlation under concurrent load or distributed cache (un-tested)
Whether result generalizes beyond Flask 3.1.3 localhost to distributed production, non-Flask frameworks, or real OAuth/CDN hierarchies
Whether headers-only structural signal (ETag+CacheControl+entropy+hash) captures sufficient variation for product freshness detection or captures too little variance (structural std 0.06-0.08)
